paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.

model_annotations.English: The chart titled “QAdapter” illustrates GPU memory usage for several fine-tuning approaches, shown as a single-series vertical bar chart. The category axis is the horizontal x-axis, with six method labels displayed diagonally: “Full FT,” “MTL-FT,” “TAG,” “Adapter,” “QAdapter,” and “Ours” (with “Ours” visually emphasized in bold italic styling). The value axis is the vertical y-axis labeled “GPU Memory (GB),” shown on a linear scale with numeric ticks at approximately 0, 20, 40, and 60 GB (the plotting area extends above 60 to accommodate the tallest bar). Each method is represented by one solid bar: “Full FT” is an orange bar reaching roughly the low-70s GB (about 72 GB), “MTL-FT” is orange at roughly the low-40s GB (about 43 GB), “TAG” is orange just under 20 GB (about 19 GB), “Adapter” is orange around the high-teens GB (about 17 GB), “QAdapter” is orange around single-digit GB (about 8 GB), and “Ours” is a green bar near 20 GB (about 19 GB). The bars are not shown as grouped or stacked, there is no legend, and no numerical annotations appear on the bars; the categories appear in the displayed left-to-right order without an indicated sorting rule.
model_annotations.German: The chart titled “QAdapter” illustrates GPU memory usage for several fine-tuning approaches, with each method represented by a single vertical bar. The horizontal axis lists categorical methods (left to right) as Full FT, MTL-FT, TAG, Adapter, QAdapter, and Ours, shown as diagonally rotated labels; “Ours” appears visually emphasized with larger/bolder text. The vertical axis is labeled “GPU Memory (GB)” and uses a linear scale with labeled ticks at 0, 20, 40, and 60 GB, extending to a maximum a little above 70 GB. Five baseline bars are colored orange: Full FT is the tallest at roughly 72–73 GB, MTL-FT is about 42–43 GB, TAG is about 19 GB, Adapter is about 16–17 GB, and QAdapter is about 8–9 GB. The final bar for Ours is colored green and is approximately 19 GB. The bars are presented as a single series (no grouping or stacking), and there are no value annotations; the methods are arranged in the stated left-to-right order rather than being strictly sorted by bar height.
